OpenRevelare — 彩色负片去色罩工具（复刻 NegativeConv:
OpenRevelare — colour-negative mask removal (a port of NegativeConvert).

How a roll goes through:
1. File → New roll… (Ctrl+N) and pick one or more negatives (several = one roll); the film strip on the left switches frames.
2. Roll calibration (Stage 1):
   · Sample the film base to take the orange mask off; sample or auto-detect D_max for the white end.
   · White balance with wb_offset (additive, shadows) / wb_high (multiplicative, highlights), or use “Brightest = white / Deep white balance”.
   · Contrast = paper grade (soft / normal / hard / manual grade+pivot).
   · Lens correction (distortion / vignetting / LCC flat field) and the sprocket mask.
3. Frame edit (Stage 2): temperature/tint, exposure, black and white points, shadows/highlights, contrast, saturation, tone curve.
4. Apply to the whole roll (button at the foot of the panel) / copy and apply to ticked frames (the Edit menu, or right-click in the film strip);
   “Choose what to sync” decides which fields travel.
5. File → Export this frame… (Ctrl+E) / Export roll… / Export contact sheet…
   (16-bit TIFF with ICC; the arrow beside the export button opens the same three)
   Fill in “Roll info” on the right of the contact-sheet window (camera/film/ISO/roll no./lab/process/date/location/notes);
   it is burned onto the foot of the sheet as one identification strip. Never written to EXIF.

Right-click menus:
· Preview — zoom, view the negative, before/after, crop, rotate and flip, backdrop colour.
· Film strip — add images, make a virtual copy, remove from the roll, copy/apply calibration and scene.

Keys:
F fit to window · Ctrl+1 actual pixels · N view the negative · K before/after · Esc cancel sampling
Ctrl+Z/Y undo·redo · Ctrl+N new roll · Ctrl+O add images · Ctrl+E export
Ctrl+Shift+T light/dark theme · Ctrl+, preferences

Sampling: light up a sampling button (the dashed-rectangle icon), then drag a box on the preview; Esc cancels.
Sliders: double-click the label to put it back to its default.
Drag with the left button to pan once zoomed; the wheel zooms.
